# Jobs

## Jobs
- Supervisor for Pods - Carrying out Batch Tasks
- Manages Task Execution
- Tracks Task Progress
- Retries Tasks as Required

## CronJobs
- Time Based Job Schedulers
- Uses the Traditional Unix CronJob Scheduling System
- Run Tasks on a Schedule
- Create Job Objects as per a Schedule

CronJob (API Object)
- Defines the schedule (using cron syntax) and the job template.
- Responsible for when and how often something should run.

Job (Object) 
- Each scheduled run of a CronJob spawns a Job
- A job represents a one-time execution of the specified task.

Pod (Workload)
- A Job, in turn, creates one or more Pods to actually do the work
- Pods run on nodes and execute the container image you defined

Job Completion & History
- Once the Pod finishes, the Job reports completion
- The CronJob controller records the history of executions (both successful and failed), which can be turned via `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` and `failedJobsHistoryLimit`.

Understanding this lifecycle is key: when debugging or monitoring a CronJob, you often need to inspect not just the CronJob itself, but also the Job and Pods it spawns.


## Lab

### Jobs

Create a job to calculate pi using the perl image

```sh
kubectl create job calculatepi --image=perl:5.34.0 -- "perl" "-Mbignum=bpi" "-wle" "print bpi(2000)"
```

Output:

```sh
job.batch/calculatepi created
```

And watch the job completion, can take up to 60 seconds, press ctrl-c to exit:

```sh
watch kubectl get jobs
```

Output:

```sh
Every 2.0s: kubectl get jobs                                                                                                                                                     control-plane: Wed Jan 21 08:29:07 2026

NAME          STATUS     COMPLETIONS   DURATION   AGE
calculatepi   Complete   1/1           48s        90s
```

If we run a describe against this job, we cna see that this completed:

```sh
kubectl describe job/calculatepi
```

Let's capture the pod name

```sh
PI_POD=$(kubectl get pods | grep calculatepi | awk {'print $1'}); echo $PI_POD
```

Output:

```sh
calculatepi-ct9ln
```

And lets view the logs from the pod, showing pi to 2000 places:

```sh
kubectl logs $PI_POD
```

Output:

```sh
3.
```

Let's delete this job

```sh
kubectl delete job/calculatepi
```

We'll capture the yaml from our pi job to a file called calculatepi

```sh
kubectl create job calculatepi --image=perl:5.34.0 --dry-run=client -o yaml -- "perl" "-Mbignum=bpi" "-wle" "print bpi(2000)" | tee calculatepi.yaml
```

Output:

```sh
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: calculatepi
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - perl
        - -Mbignum=bpi
        - -wle
        - print bpi(2000)
        image: perl:5.34.0
        name: calculatepi
        resources: {}
      restartPolicy: Never
status: {}
```

Update the calculatepi.yaml to include completions of 20 and parallelism of 5

```sh
cat <<EOF > calculatepi.yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: calculatepi
spec:
  completions: 20
  parallelism: 5
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - perl
        - -Mbignum=bpi
        - -wle
        - print bpi(2000)
        image: perl:5.34.0
        name: calculatepi
        resources: {}
      restartPolicy: Never
status: {}
EOF
```

Apply this file, we'll add a small sleep and will watch the output of kubectl get pods, this will run until we have 20 pods with up to 5 pods at any time

```sh
kubectl apply -f calculatepi.yaml && sleep 1 && watch kubectl get pods -o wide
```

Output:

```sh

We could from any of these pods, get the logs and see pi calculated

```sh
PI_POD=$(kubectl get pods | grep calculatepi | tail -1 | awk {'print $1'}); kubectl logs $PI_POD
```

```

Remove the job, this will also delete all of the associated pods

``sh
kubectl delete job/calculatepi
```

Ouput:

```sh
job.batch "calculatepi" deleted
```

If we check, all of these pods have been removed

```sh
kubectl get pods -o wide
```

Output:

```sh
No resources found in default namespace
```

Let's cleanup, the yaml file:

```sh
rm calculatepi.yaml
```

### CronJobs

We'll re-use the previous example but we will repurpose it as a CronJob with a schedule of * * * * * (every minute)-

```sh
kubectl create cronjob calculatepi --image=perl:5.34.0 --schedule="* * * * *" -- "perl" "-Mbignum=bpi" "-wle" "print bpi(2000)"
```

Output:

```sh
cronjob.batch/calculatepi created
```

If we watch this, as the minute ticks over it should start, you may need to toggle the tutorial button to close this pane to see this, press ctrl-c to exit

```sh
watch kubectl get jobs
```

Output:

```sh
Every 2.0s: kubectl get jobs                                                                                                                                                     control-plane: Wed Jan 21 08:50:03 2026

NAME                   STATUS     COMPLETIONS   DURATION   AGE
calculatepi-29483089   Complete   1/1           13s        63s
calculatepi-29483090   Running    0/1           3s         3s
```

Regardless of how many jobs are completed, we will only have 3 running in total, it may briefly step up to 4 but then it will go back to 3.

This is because of the successfulJobsHistoryLimit parameter. You can see this by running an edit on the job, whilst here, add in completions:20 and parallelism: 5 under spec.jobTemplate.spec, save the file and exit when done

```sh
# Please edit the object below. Lines beginning with a '#' will be ignored,
# and an empty file will abort the edit. If an error occurs while saving this file will be
# reopened with the relevant failures.
#
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2026-01-21T08:48:17Z"
  generation: 1
  name: calculatepi
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "2022"
  uid: 8c05d5c0-8328-4d8b-a6bd-f4e78775b075
spec:
  concurrencyPolicy: Allow
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      name: calculatepi
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          creationTimestamp: null
        spec:
          containers:
          - command:
            - perl
            - -Mbignum=bpi
            - -wle
            - print bpi(2000)
            image: perl:5.34.0
            imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
            name: calculatepi
            resources: {}
            terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
            terminationMessagePolicy: File
          dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          schedulerName: default-scheduler
          securityContext: {}
          terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
  schedule: '* * * * *'
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  suspend: false
status:
  lastScheduleTime: "2026-01-21T08:51:00Z"
  lastSuccessfulTime: "2026-01-21T08:51:11Z"
